learningObjective: Diagnose memory-bandwidth-bound decode from profile data and identify effective vs ineffective mitigations.
stem: The following profile is collected for a single decode step at batch size 1 on a Llama-2-13B model on A100 80GB. Which mitigations are consistent with the bottleneck and select those that would concretely reduce TPOT. (Choose all that apply.)
profileData:
Model: Llama-2-13B, FP16 weights.
  Per decode step (batch=1):
    HBM read for weights: 26 GB / step, elapsed 13 ms → effective bandwidth ≈ 2000 GB/s (close to A100 peak ~2 TB/s)
    HBM read for KV cache: 200 MB / step, elapsed 0.1 ms
    SM compute utilization inside kernels: 22%
    Kernel launch gaps: ~10% of step time
    TPOT (this step): ~14.5 ms

options.text: Continuous batching that raises the effective batch size (multiple requests decoded together) would amortize the same weight read across all requests, cutting TPOT-per-request substantially when the amortized batch is large enough (moving the operator toward compute-bound).

Adding tensor-core-accelerated math kernels for the MLP GEMMs would raise SM utilization from 22% to near 100% and cut TPOT proportionally, because the low utilization directly indicates undersubscribed compute.
CUDA Graph capture of the decode step would eliminate most of the 10% launch-gap fraction, cutting TPOT by roughly that amount (a modest but real improvement).

Weight-only INT4 quantization would cut weight HBM reads by ~4x, reducing the weight-read time (dominant cost) by close to a factor of 4 and directly cutting TPOT — subject to available INT4 GEMM kernels and acceptable accuracy loss.

explanation: The signature is memory-bandwidth-bound decode: weight reads dominate (13 ms of 14.5 ms), effective bandwidth is already near peak, and SM utilization is low because the kernels are bandwidth-bound. Real levers are (A) reducing weight bytes (quantization) — biggest lever; (B) sharing weight reads across a batch (continuous batching / batched decode); (D) reducing launch overhead (CUDA Graphs) — small but real. (C) is wrong: 22% utilization is a symptom of being memory-bound, not undersubscribed compute; adding math capability does not help a bandwidth-bound kernel.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: amortize weight reads across batch.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: reverses diagnosis; low utilization is expected for bandwidth-bound.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: bandwidth-bound → cut bytes; INT4 is the standard lever.

assumptions: INT4 kernels are available and accuracy loss is acceptable.
Multiple concurrent requests are available for batching.
nonImplications: Does not imply INT4 is quality-neutral.
Does not imply CUDA Graphs are compatible with all shape configurations.

performanceClaim.scope: Decode bandwidth-bound diagnosis and effective mitigations
